children: Crude oil rose above $100 a barrel on Thursday, reaching its highest level since May 19, as escalating tensions in the Middle East raised fears of prolonged disruption to global energy supplies.
Iran signalled it will continue retaliatory strikes if US attacks persist, while Iran-backed Houthi forces are targeting Saudi assets and threatening shipping routes.
Saudi Arabia’s crude oil production fell sharply in August 2026, dropping by around 1.9 million barrels a day to 6.238 million barrels a day, its lowest level since 1990.
The deteriorating backdrop from the Middle East dims expectations that supply from the region could be normalized as Asian economies are forced to re-enter the energy market.

China imported 8.93 bpd of crude oil in August, a 6.2% increase from July, after its reliance on inventory since the start of the conflict shielded the global economy from a deeper energy shortage due to blockaded tankers in the Persian Gulf.

title: Crude Oil Tops $100
